LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Project consists of the construction of a 11.6MW (gross) waste to energy (WTE) plant located on 4.8 hectares of land in the Thuan Thanh district of Bac Ninh province, approximately 40 km east of Hanoi, Vietnam. The Project will generate income from waste tipping fees and from power sold to the national grid via a 20-year power purchase agreement with Electricity of Vietnam (EVN). The Project will be developed, constructed, and operated by T&J Green Energy Company Limited (T&J), a company jointly invested by local company Thuan Thanh Environment JSC (TT) and by JFE Engineering Corporation (JFEE) of Japan.,The main project-level outcomes are the stakeholder impact via the increase in waste treatment capacity that will help reduce health and safety risks in the community, and the environmental impact via the avoidance of greenhouse gas emissions from methane emissions generated by the decomposition of waste in landfills and the generating of renewable power. The expected market-level impact is from improved sustainability by supporting the development of one of the first WTE plants in the country.

Rapid urbanization coupled with population growth have led to an increase in municipal solid waste (MSW) generation in Viet Nam to unmanageable levels. During the period 2004 2015, waste generation increased by about 87% from 15 million tons per year (MT/y) to about 28 MT/y by 2015. Significant portion of the waste collected are disposed at landfills within 200-500 meters of residential areas. Less than 30% of those sites are classified as engineered or sanitary landfills. This poses a significant threat for public health in areas where there is high level of waste generation due to the contamination of the ground and surface water by untreated leachate, emissions of airborne pollutants, and the spread of flies, mosquitoes, rodents and dust.

LONG_DESCRIPTION: This investment builds on the Mekong Inclusion Project Phase I (2014/15-2019/20) currently being implemented by Oxfam Australia. It will be supporting civil society partners, women leaders and communities in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam and at the regional level, to engage with and influence governments, inter-governmental bodies and the private sector in water resource governance, planning and development. Using the tools and experience from IP1, IP2 will work more directly with private sectors, financiers and governments to enhance accountability in the hydropower sector but also broaden the activities to include community engagement in policy discussions on alternative energy sources. SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SUPPORT FOR REALIZING LARGE PRIVATE SECTOR WASTE-TO-ENERGY INITIATIVE IN NORTHERN VIETNAM
PROJECT_TITLE: Support for realizing large private sector Waste-to-Energy initiative in Northern Vietnam
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Project will establish a waste to energy (W2E) plant for provincial scale municipal waste treatment in Phu Lang ward Que Vo district Bac Ninh prov-ince (semi-urban area). The Project site is a 5-hectare plot leased from the government. Civil works started early 2019. The plot is located close to the Câu river and existing landfills. The investment license land-use license and environmental permit have been granted.The Project will receive municipal solid waste delivered by a local municipal waste management company process it into RDF incinerate it to generate electricity to be fed to the grid operated by the state-owned EVN. The design capacity of the plant is 500 tons of municipal solid waste/day for an electricity production of 10MWe. In addition to municipal solid waste the plant will use some industrial waste. The incineration will use a Circulating Fluidized Boiler (CFB) technology from Finland with emission abatement and effluent treat-ment.The Project includes: -Waste to energy (W2E) plant: waste receiving sorting and processing waste incineration turbine and generator-Fresh water supply system for the W2E Plant including water treatment system-Construction of overhead power lines and stations to evacuate the power to the grid (EVN)-Other facilities such as storage bunkers ash handling effluent treatment plant emission abatement systems-Waste supply chain (Provincial waste management body)The beneficiary organisatoin is Thang Long Energy Environment JSC and the EPC contractor is a major local company. International Cleantech Ventures Finland Ltd (ICVF) has prepared a feasibility study for the project in 2017 how-ever the relevance of the feasibility study is limited due to e.g. alteration of the scope and capacity of the plant. This project is aimed at assessing the Environmental Social and Technical impacts and implications of the Plant.
